From the surgery

From the surgery

Reflections from a family doctor on what psychology brings to primary care.

Primary care shows every day how body and mind intertwine: insomnia that begins with grief, pain that worsens with stress, worry that leads to requests for tests, the loneliness of many older people. This section will gather short texts, written from that experience, linking those situations to what psychology knows.

If a case is ever mentioned, it will be anonymised and altered so that no one can be recognised.

Sleeping badly is not always a sleep problem

Insomnia is one of the most common complaints in the surgery. Behind it there are often worries, life changes or habits, and the first recommended treatment is not a pill.

Loneliness needs care too

Unwanted loneliness affects physical and mental health. Primary care is a good place to detect it and to connect people with their community.
